finding.old_claim: A deterministic tool_use_id-to-agent_id join is not established by current documentation alone because Agent-specific tool_response identity is unknown.
finding.corrected_claim: Current official Claude Code hook documentation gives PostToolUse a call-scoped tool_use_id and documents the Agent tool's PostToolUse tool_response as containing agentId. Therefore the same documented PostToolUse event supplies a deterministic specification-level pair tool_use_id -> tool_response.agentId. This closes the tool invocation to Agent-response identity gap at documentation/capability scope only.
finding.still_open: SubagentStart/SubagentStop use the field name agent_id. Exact installed-runtime evidence is still required to prove the emitted Agent tool_response.agentId and lifecycle agent_id normalize to the same child identity on the target build/configuration. Hook firing, plugin/host configuration, concurrency behavior and durable package_id linkage remain runtime-unverified.
finding.task_identity: TaskCreated/TaskCompleted task_id remains a separate task-system identity and must stay optional for ordinary Agent-subagent execution unless that task lifecycle is actually observed.

external_primary.scope: PostToolUse common input includes tool_use_id; Agent-specific tool_response contains agentId; SubagentStart/SubagentStop lifecycle exposes agent_id; TaskCreated/TaskCompleted exposes task_id.
Agent is the native subagent execution surface described by current documentation.

rules: Do not use timestamp or event order as a concurrency join when call-scoped identity exists.
Preserve camelCase agentId and snake_case agent_id as separate source fields until an installed-runtime receipt demonstrates their identity relationship.
Do not require task_id for ordinary Agent execution unless TaskCreated/TaskCompleted is observed in that path.
A documentation-level join is capability/spec evidence, not installed-host runtime proof.

packet_disposition.reason: The prior quarantine remains correct because the packet still has stale canonical-main binding, an invalid target_2_0_action enum, and a wrong governance source span. This correction only narrows one external-documentation unknown.
